title: Testing, Debugging & Logging
intro: Learn the basic ideas of Testing, Debugging & Logging in simple English. Read the explanation and example first; the quiz asks only from the concepts taught here.

items.heading: Testing
items.text: Testing checks whether code behaves as expected. Automated tests can be run repeatedly after changes.

items.heading: Unit test
items.text: A unit test checks a small, focused unit of code such as a function.

items.heading: assert
items.text: assert checks that a condition is true and raises an error when it is false.

items.heading: Debugging
items.text: Debugging is the process of finding and fixing problems in a program.

items.heading: Breakpoint
items.text: A breakpoint pauses program execution so you can inspect variables and program state.

items.heading: Traceback
items.text: A traceback shows where an exception occurred and helps locate the failing code.

items.heading: Logging
items.text: Logging records useful runtime information that can help understand what a program is doing.

items.heading: Log levels
items.text: Levels such as DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR and CRITICAL classify the importance of messages.

items.heading: Regression
items.text: A regression happens when a change breaks behavior that previously worked. Tests help catch regressions.

items.heading: Investigating failures
items.text: A failing test is information: inspect the failure, reproduce it, find the cause and fix the underlying problem.

items.heading: Protect secrets
items.text: Logs should not expose passwords, API keys or other sensitive values.
